children: Sydney-based investment manager New Forests acquired the entire share capital of Rance Timber, a 116-year-old Eastern Cape forestry and sawmilling company, ending more than a century of ownership by the founding Rance family,
Daily Investor
reported, citing the bank that advised the sellers. The price was not disclosed.

New Forests first announced its investment in Rance Timber in September 2025. At the time, it was reported to have taken a majority stake, and its Africa managing director, Yida Kemoli, said the family would retain a partnership position,
Impact Investor

reported. A case study published on October 20 by Standard Bank, which advised the sellers, now describes the deal as the disposal by shareholder Famran Investments of Rance Timber’s entire issued share capital. Famran previously bought shares in the group’s forestry holding company, according to a 2017 presentation to parliament’s agriculture committee. The two accounts conflict: it is unclear whether the 2025 reports of a majority stake were inaccurate or whether the family kept an indirect interest through another entity.
Succession sale

Founded by HC Rance in 1910, the company had been owned by four generations of the family. Standard Bank said family members were approaching retirement without a clear succession plan and wanted to realise the value of the business while protecting its future. Two earlier attempts to sell the company had failed, the bank said, before it ran a competitive process that looked beyond the most obvious local buyers.

“Family-owned businesses are the backbone of our economy, but they face unique pressures,” said Raven Moodley, head of corporate finance advisory for Standard Bank South Africa’s business and commercial banking division.

“Rance conducted a thorough process to find an investor who will continue Rance’s philosophy of careful stewardship of its human and natural resources,” Chris Rance, the company’s finance director and a shareholder, said when the deal was announced in 2025.
Plantations and sawmills

Rance Timber is a vertically integrated business spanning plantations, harvesting, sawmilling and timber sales, based near Stutterheim in the Amathole district. It runs two sawmills, Kubusi and Sandile, which produce structural timber for South Africa’s building industry. At the time of the 2025 announcement it employed about 1,400 people across its forestry and sawmilling divisions, according to New Forests.
New Forests described the business in 2025 as managing more than 14,000 hectares of pine plantations, while
Daily Investor
put the figure at 15,000 hectares. Plantations make up almost 60% of the area, with the rest indigenous forest, grassland, riparian zones and other protected vegetation, New Forests said.

The plantations are held by Amathole Forestry Company, a former state forestry business privatised in 2005. That year, Rance and its black economic empowerment partners won a public tender to buy a majority stake in the company, which leases its land from the state, according to FSC Africa. The state-owned South African Forestry Company still held 16% of Amathole Forestry on behalf of communities, according to its 2022/23 annual report. Neither New Forests nor Standard Bank has said how the Amathole stake was treated in the sale, so it is unclear whether all of the plantation area passed to New Forests.
Impact fund’s first South African deal

The deal was made through New Forests’ African Forestry Impact Platform (AFIP), an open-ended vehicle launched in 2022 with British International Investment, Norfund and Finnfund to invest in plantation forestry companies in sub-Saharan Africa. Rance Timber was AFIP’s second investment and New Forests’ first in South Africa, following AFIP’s acquisition of Green Resources in East Africa.
The acquisition expanded New Forests’ sub-Saharan portfolio to more than 52,000 hectares of plantations across South Africa, Mozambique, Tanzania and Uganda,
Agri Investor
reported at the time. Kemoli said New Forests planned to focus on carbon, biodiversity, local livelihoods and gender equity at the business.
Although headquartered in Sydney, New Forests is owned mainly by Japan’s Mitsui & Co. and Nomura, which agreed in 2022 to take stakes of about 49% and 41% respectively,
IPE Real Assets
reported. The purchase was completed in January 2023, according to a notice from New Zealand’s overseas investment regulator.

title: New Forests buys South Africa’s Rance Timber, over a century of family ownership
